faqs.q: What challenges did you face in your projects?
faqs.a: Across projects, the key challenges were: shaping time-series data for the LSTM in the Apple Stock Prediction system, generating meaningful recommendations with limited history in the Product Recommendation System, designing clean REST/CRUD flows for the Job Tracker API, and consolidating scattered SQL/Excel sources for the Sales Dashboard. Each was solved with verified, project-specific techniques described in the project details.

faqs.q: Explain the toughest part of the Apple Stock project.
faqs.a: The hardest part was preparing sequential market data for LSTM training and keeping predictions stable against noisy fluctuations. It was solved with preprocessing, normalization, sliding-window sequence generation, proper train-test splitting, feature scaling and regression-metric evaluation before visualising forecasts in Streamlit.

faqs.q: Explain challenges in the Recommendation System.
faqs.a: Two main challenges: generating meaningful recommendations for users with limited interaction history, and balancing accuracy with response performance. Solved by implementing similarity-based collaborative filtering with Scikit-learn and optimising the Pandas/NumPy preprocessing and vectorised similarity logic for efficient top-N results.

faqs.q: What challenges did you face in the Job Tracker API?
faqs.a: Designing a clean REST contract for job-application CRUD and persisting data reliably. Solved by structuring Flask routes around a single resource with clear status codes, a MySQL schema for storage and request validation with predictable error handling.

faqs.q: What challenges did you face in the Sales Dashboard?
faqs.a: Consolidating scattered SQL and Excel sources into one trustworthy model, and making the report self-serve for non-technical stakeholders. Solved by cleaning and modelling data in Power BI with consistent KPIs, then designing KPI cards and interactive slicers by product, region and period.

faqs.q: What did you learn from the Apple Stock Price Prediction project?
faqs.a: He learned the end-to-end time-series forecasting workflow, how to build and train LSTM models in TensorFlow/Keras, the importance of normalization and sequence generation, regression evaluation with RMSE/MAE, and how to deploy an ML application with Streamlit.

faqs.q: What did you learn from the Product Recommendation System project?
faqs.a: He learned collaborative filtering and similarity-based recommendation techniques, how to evaluate recommendation quality, data preprocessing and feature engineering with Pandas/NumPy, and how recommendation systems improve user experience in real-world applications.

faqs.q: What did you learn from the Job Tracker API project?
faqs.a: He learned how to design RESTful CRUD endpoints with Flask, separate routing from data access, model relational data in MySQL, validate JSON requests and return consistent error responses, and manage the full API request lifecycle.

faqs.q: What did you learn from the Sales Dashboard project?
faqs.a: He learned how to import, clean and model SQL/Excel data in Power BI, define business KPIs and calculated measures, build interactive slicers for self-service analysis, and design visuals that communicate insights to non-technical stakeholders.

faqs.q: What did you learn from your projects?
faqs.a: Across projects, he learned end-to-end machine learning pipelines (LSTM time-series forecasting and Scikit-learn recommendation systems), REST API design with Flask and MySQL, and business intelligence reporting with Power BI, SQL and Excel.

faqs.q: What skills did this project help you develop?
faqs.a: Each project strengthened specific skills: the Apple Stock project developed deep-learning and time-series modelling; the Recommendation System developed collaborative filtering and feature engineering; the Job Tracker API developed Flask, REST design and MySQL; and the Sales Dashboard developed Power BI, KPI design and data storytelling.

Mahesh's learning has been project-driven: he built ML models in Python (LSTM, recommendation systems), developed backend APIs with Flask and MySQL, and created business dashboards with Power BI and SQL. Every project focused on practical, recruiter-relevant skills for Data Analyst and MIS Executive roles.

LSTM was selected for the Apple Stock Price Prediction System because LSTM networks are designed to learn long-term dependencies in sequential time-series data, which is essential for forecasting stock prices from historical market data.

TensorFlow and Keras were chosen to build and train the LSTM deep-learning model in the Apple Stock project because they provide a simple, scalable API for prototyping and productionizing neural networks.

Streamlit was used in both the Apple Stock Price Prediction System and the Product Recommendation System to quickly build interactive web interfaces for visualizing predictions and recommendations without building a full frontend stack.
Collaborative filtering was used in the Product Recommendation System to generate personalized product suggestions based on user behavior and similarity patterns in the interaction data.
Python was selected across all projects because of its rich ecosystem for data analysis, machine learning, recommendation algorithms, backend API development and rapid prototyping.
Pandas was used in the Apple Stock and Product Recommendation projects for efficient cleaning, transformation, preprocessing and manipulation of structured datasets.
Flask was chosen for the Job Tracker API because it is a lightweight Python micro-framework that keeps the API focused, extensible and easy to maintain.
MySQL was selected for the Job Tracker API to provide reliable, structured relational storage for job-application records and to support consistent SQL querying.
Power BI was selected for the Sales Dashboard because it is an industry-standard BI platform for building interactive, self-service sales visuals and KPI reporting.
